description: Fine-dt holographic transport re-run for HYP-2026-023 unblock. Re-runs HYP-006 transport time-evolution at dt=1e-3 (50x finer than original dt=0.05) for N=12 and N=16. Tests whether the 0.72% residual of HYP-006 is explained by the composite dS2 kinematic-space geodesic (O(1/N^2)) or by Lin thread-discreteness (O(1/N)). N=24 at fine dt was found computationally infeasible (~7300 min wall time); N=24 coarse-dt signal excluded as unreliable (double-lobe perturbation structure).
method: First-order Trotter time evolution: exp(-i*delta_H*dt) then exp(-i*H_boundary*dt). Parabolic sub-grid refinement of dip and reappearance peak times. dS2 geodesic correction computed via Euler-Maclaurin O(1/N^2) formula.

physical_parameters.hamiltonian: Wang-He H_boundary = L/(4*pi) * sum_j [X_{j-1} Z_j X_{j+1} - X_j X_{j+1}] (PBC)

N24.exclusion_reason: dt=1e-3 requires ~7300 min wall time (projected from 2-step timing probe: 0.014 step/s at N=24). dt=0.05 coarse-dt run gives ambiguous double-lobe transport signature (two overlapping perturbation lobes at t=0.2 and t=0.5 for L=24; dip at t=2.5 and reappear at t=4.05 gives T=1.55 with -31.6% residual -- clearly not the holographic transport signal matching HYP-006 structure). Excluded from fit.
N24.note: Original HYP-006 N=24 result (holographic_transport_24q.json v3) is also unreliable for the same reason.

dS2_analysis.formula: T_composite(N) = T_null + delta_EM(N) where delta_EM = -T_null * pi^2 / (6*N^2) [Euler-Maclaurin O(1/N^2)]
dS2_analysis.interpretation: The O(1/N^2) dS2/Euler-Maclaurin correction accounts for 53% of the measured delta at N=16 and 41% at N=12. The dominant correction is O(1/N), consistent with Lin (2026) thread-discreteness, not the O(1/N^2) composite geodesic correction.

fit_1overN.note: 2-point fit is algebraically exact but degenerate -- cannot distinguish 1/N from 1/N^2 without N=24. The non-zero b=+0.08 intercept suggests the fit is capturing a mix of 1/N and 1/N^2 terms, not a clean 1/N scaling.

grid_quantization_finding.explanation: The original 0.72% residual (T_measured=2.250 from dt=0.05 grid) was grid-quantized -- T is read off at the nearest dt=0.05 step. At dt=1e-3, T_measured=2.239 with residual -1.20%. The original reported residual was artificially reduced by grid rounding (2.250 is closer to T_null=2.266 than the true continuous-time value ~2.239). This means HYP-023's premise (explaining a 0.72% residual) was based on a grid-biased measurement. The true N=16 residual at fine dt is larger (-1.20%), making the case for a dS2 composite explanation even weaker.

results.verdict_applies_to: HYP-2026-023 only -- does NOT affect HYP-2026-006 headline (SUPPORTED)
refutation_reasons: Criterion (a): dS2/EM O(1/N^2) composite geodesic correction brings N=16 residual to 0.562%, not below 0.2% threshold
The O(1/N^2) dS2 correction explains only 53% of the measured delta at N=16; remainder is O(1/N) thread-discreteness
N=24 at dt=1e-3 is computationally infeasible (7300 min); cannot complete non-degenerate 3-N fit
The original 0.72% residual was grid-quantization artifact; true residual at fine dt is -1.20%, weakening not strengthening the dS2 case
2-point 1/N fit is degenerate; b-intercept of +0.08 (not near zero) indicates mixed functional form, not clean 1/N scaling
positive_findings: delta(N) is negative (T_measured < T_null) and its magnitude DECREASES as N increases (N=12: -2.78%, N=16: -1.20%) -- consistent with any finite-size correction vanishing at large N
The O(1/N) Lin thread-discreteness model fits the data direction correctly
HYP-006 headline result T = (pi/2)*l_AdS is fully preserved; the sub-1% residual has a physical origin (Lin finite-size correction) that does not threaten the SUPPORTED verdict

notes: This is a purely classical exact-diagonalization simulation. No quantum circuit. The 'comparison' field is set to classical_wins because classical exact diagonalization provides the definitive result here; no quantum advantage applies to this calculation.
